correctness.rationale: Normalizing independent Gaussian pairs in the two planes gives the uniform squared plane radius T and independent angular coordinates; conditioning on the sectors retains those properties. Distance to the complement of the hemisphere intersection is the minimum inward margin, and folding each angle chooses the lesser sine for apertures ≤π. The two inequalities on T give exactly the asserted positive interval length. Its maximum is at the two half apertures, giving q and inradius ρ. For endpoint asymptotics I bounded the positive support using convexity of csc² at fixed subhemispheric aperture and sec²(d+δ)−sec²(d)≥δ²+2dδ near the hemispheric limit, where d is the half-aperture deficit and δ the folded-angle deficit. This gives bounded rescaled domains and a rigorous dominated-convergence argument. The limiting interval lengths are the stated positive parts with linear or quadratic terms; integrating gives H³/(6c_ac_b), 4H^(5/2)/(15c_b√q), and π before the folded-angle factor 4/(αβ), hence the three coefficients. For moving d=λ√h/2, expansion of the difference of sec² values gives h(x²+λx) when δ=√h x. Centering at the moving ρ before expanding gives the two window integrals, also at zero window parameters. The description 'Gaussian-quadrant integrals' in the last proof line of this part is imprecise: these are compact positive-part polynomial integrals. For the both-hemisphere case the normalized marginal density of X₂=s≥0 is (4/π)√(1−s²), and the conditional X₄ is uniform on [0,√(1−s²)]. Differentiating both sin t cutoffs and integrating verifies the exact closed form including the endpoints. For fixed subhemispheric apertures the rescaled conditional density is constant on bounded domains whose indicators converge in L¹ to the indicator of Ω. The affine four-slack map yields uniform measure on the simplex, giving the claimed TV convergence and Dirichlet limit. Full analytic replay: /workspace/calculations/geometric_checks.md. The frozen quadrature code was inspected, not executed; finite samples are not certificates for the limits.
